paras.text: Table sugar or cane sugar is the generally available form of sucrose. Sucrose is a disaccharide. Sucrose is a combination of fructose (fruit sugar) and glucose (simple plant sugar). Sucrose is a popular sweeting agent. It is used in healthy sweets, soft drinks and energy drinks. Sucrose is a caloric carbohydrate and thus is efficient to provide energy. 1 gram of sucrose produces 4 kilo calories energy when metabolises.

paras.text: Lactose is the disaccharide naturally found in milk. It is composed of glucose and galactose. Human milk contains 7.2% lactose while cow milk contains about 4.8% lactose. Milk is a universal food of new born mammals and one of the most complete human diets. Although glucose could be found in several types of foods, lactose is the only source of galactose.

paras.text: The main disadvantage associated with lactose (glactose) is that many human adults are unable to digest milk due to deficiency of lactase, (Lactase is an enzyme, splits lactose into glucose and galactose) which is called lactose-intolerance. Lactose intolerance is the inability to digest lactose that results in intestinal discomfort such as, cramps, flatulence, colic pains, abnormal intestinal flow, nausea and watery diarrhoea. These symptoms appear within 30-90 minutes after the ingestion of milk. It is important to remind that lactose intolerance is not a disease but a condition. To avoid this, fermented milk products such as yogurt and cheese should be used.

paras.text: Glucose is a simple carbohydrate. It is the most common and popular monosaccharide that can be found in sweet fruits such as grapes, which contains 20 – 30 % glucose. The carbohydrates you eat are converted to glucose in the body. The concentration of glucose in the blood, referred to as the blood glucose level, is vital to the proper functioning of the human body.

paras.text: Human pancreas secretes a hormone known as insulin. Insulin helps in the metabolism of glucose to produce energy. In some cases, defects in the metabolism of glucose occurs due to which blood glucose level rise from the normal level. This condition results in a disease known as diabetes mellitus. The consequences of unchecked diabetes include hardening of blood vessels, dysfunction of kidney, diabetic coma that causes premature death.

paras.text: 21.2 Proteins

paras.text: The term protein is derived from the Greek word proteios, which means “first, prime or chief”. Proteins are naturally occurring polymers composed of amino acid units joined to one another by amide (or peptide) bonds. Spider webs, animal hair and muscle, egg whites and haemoglobin (the molecule that transports oxygen in the body to where it is needed) are all proteins. They are present in all animals, plants, bacteria and viruses.

Role of Various Carbohydrates in Health and Disease

There are different types of carbohydrates, which are involved in the health and diseases of living beings. Some of these are given below.

1. Sucrose

Table sugar or cane sugar is the generally available form of sucrose. Sucrose is a disaccharide. Sucrose is a combination of fructose (fruit sugar) and glucose (simple plant sugar). Sucrose is a popular sweeting agent. It is used in healthy sweets, soft drinks and energy drinks. Sucrose is a caloric carbohydrate and thus is efficient to provide energy. 1 gram of sucrose produces 4 kilo calories energy when metabolises.

Excess of sucrose may cause some problems such as,

Tooth decay

Obesity

Plaque formation upon our teeth

Gum diseases

2. Lactose

Lactose is the disaccharide naturally found in milk. It is composed of glucose and galactose. Human milk contains 7.2% lactose while cow milk contains about 4.8% lactose. Milk is a universal food of new born mammals and one of the most complete human diets. Although glucose could be found in several types of foods, lactose is the only source of galactose.

Some of the important benefits of lactose (galactose) are,

Galactose has various biological functions and serves in neural and immunological processes.

Galactose is a component of several macromolecules, which are important constituents of nerve cells membrane.

Galactose is also a component of the molecules present on blood cells that determine the ABO blood types.

According to recent studies, lactose may play a role in the absorption of calcium and other minerals such as copper and zinc, especially during infancy.

The main disadvantage associated with lactose (glactose) is that many human adults are unable to digest milk due to deficiency of lactase, (Lactase is an enzyme, splits lactose into glucose and galactose) which is called lactose-intolerance. Lactose intolerance is the inability to digest lactose that results in intestinal discomfort such as, cramps, flatulence, colic pains, abnormal intestinal flow, nausea and watery diarrhoea. These symptoms appear within 30-90 minutes after the ingestion of milk. It is important to remind that lactose intolerance is not a disease but a condition. To avoid this, fermented milk products such as yogurt and cheese should be used.

3. Glucose

Glucose is a simple carbohydrate. It is the most common and popular monosaccharide that can be found in sweet fruits such as grapes, which contains 20 – 30 % glucose. The carbohydrates you eat are converted to glucose in the body. The concentration of glucose in the blood, referred to as the blood glucose level, is vital to the proper functioning of the human body.

Some of the benefits and uses of glucose are,

It is mainly used by the living bodies for the production of instant energy.

It is an important constituent of human blood, human blood contains normally about 70 – 110mg of glucose per 100cm³.

It also regulates the temperature of the body.

The surplus glucose is converted to a polymer called glycogen in human beings. Glycogen is then stored in the liver and muscles. When the body is deficient in glucose, this liver and muscle glycogen is hydrolysed to glucose according to the body requirement.

The disadvantages related to the extra intake of glucose is,

Human pancreas secretes a hormone known as insulin. Insulin helps in the metabolism of glucose to produce energy. In some cases, defects in the metabolism of glucose occurs due to which blood glucose level rise from the normal level. This condition results in a disease known as diabetes mellitus. The consequences of unchecked diabetes include hardening of blood vessels, dysfunction of kidney, diabetic coma that causes premature death.

21.2 Proteins

The term protein is derived from the Greek word proteios, which means “first, prime or chief”. Proteins are naturally occurring polymers composed of amino acid units joined to one another by amide (or peptide) bonds. Spider webs, animal hair and muscle, egg whites and haemoglobin (the molecule that transports oxygen in the body to where it is needed) are all proteins. They are present in all animals, plants, bacteria and viruses.

Chemically, proteins are complex nitrogenous organic compounds, which are associated with the concept of life itself.

By chemical composition, proteins are composed of carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen. Percentage of nitrogen is fairly constant and is about 16% of the molecular weight of protein.

دا د انسان د وینې مهمه برخه ده، د انسان وینه په عادي ډول په هر 100cm³ کې نږدې 70 – 110mg ګلوکوز لري.

دا د بدن تودوخه هم تنظیموي.

په انسانانو کې اضافي ګلوکوز په ګلایکوجن نومي پولیمر بدلېږي. بیا ګلایکوجن په ځیګر او عضلاتو کې زېرمه کېږي. کله چې بدن د ګلوکوز کمښت ولري، د ځیګر او عضلاتو دا ګلایکوجن د بدن د اړتیا سره سم ګلوکوز ته هایدرولایز کېږي.

د ګلوکوز له زیات مصرف سره تړلی زیان دا دی،

د انسان پانقراس انسولین نومی هورمون افرازوي. انسولین د انرژۍ د تولید لپاره د ګلوکوز په میټابولیزم کې مرسته کوي. په ځینو حالاتو کې د ګلوکوز په میټابولیزم کې نیمګړتیا رامنځته کېږي چې له امله یې د وینې د ګلوکوز کچه له نورمال څخه لوړېږي. دا حالت د شکرې (ډایابېټیز میلیټس) ناروغۍ ته لار هواروي. د بې کنټروله شکرې پایلو کې د وینې د رګونو کلکېدل، د پښتورګو بې دندې کېدل او د شکرې کوما شامل دي چې د وخت نه مخکې مړینې لامل کېږي.

21.2 پروټینونه

د پروټین اصطلاح له یوناني کلمې proteios اخیستل شوې چې معنا یې ”لومړی، اصلي یا مشر“ ده. پروټینونه طبیعي پولیمرونه دي چې له امینو اسید واحدونو جوړ دي چې د امایډ (یا پېپټایډ) تړونونو په واسطه له یو بل سره تړلي دي. د غڼې جالې، د ژویو وېښته او عضلات، د هګۍ سپینه او هیموګلوبین (هغه مالیکول چې په بدن کې اکسیجن اړین ځای ته رسوي) ټول پروټینونه دي. دا په ټولو ژویو، بوټو، باکتریاوو او ویروسونو کې شته.

په کیمیاوي لحاظ پروټینونه پېچلي نایټروجني عضوي مرکبات دي چې پخپله د ژوند له مفهوم سره تړلي دي.

د کیمیاوي ترکیب له مخې پروټینونه له کاربن، هایدروجن، اکسیجن او نایټروجن جوړ دي. د نایټروجن سلنه نسبتاً ثابته ده او د پروټین د مالیکولي وزن نږدې 16% ده.

Role of Various Carbohydrates in Health and Disease

There are different types of carbohydrates, which are involved in the health and diseases of living beings. Some of these are given below.

1. Sucrose

Table sugar or cane sugar is the generally available form of sucrose. Sucrose is a disaccharide. Sucrose is a combination of fructose (fruit sugar) and glucose (simple plant sugar). Sucrose is a popular sweeting agent. It is used in healthy sweets, soft drinks and energy drinks. Sucrose is a caloric carbohydrate and thus is efficient to provide energy. 1 gram of sucrose produces 4 kilo calories energy when metabolises.

Excess of sucrose may cause some problems such as,

Tooth decay

Obesity

Plaque formation upon our teeth

Gum diseases

2. Lactose

Lactose is the disaccharide naturally found in milk. It is composed of glucose and galactose. Human milk contains 7.2% lactose while cow milk contains about 4.8% lactose. Milk is a universal food of new born mammals and one of the most complete human diets. Although glucose could be found in several types of foods, lactose is the only source of galactose.

Some of the important benefits of lactose (galactose) are,

Galactose has various biological functions and serves in neural and immunological processes.

Galactose is a component of several macromolecules, which are important constituents of nerve cells membrane.

Galactose is also a component of the molecules present on blood cells that determine the ABO blood types.

According to recent studies, lactose may play a role in the absorption of calcium and other minerals such as copper and zinc, especially during infancy.

The main disadvantage associated with lactose (glactose) is that many human adults are unable to digest milk due to deficiency of lactase, (Lactase is an enzyme, splits lactose into glucose and galactose) which is called lactose-intolerance. Lactose intolerance is the inability to digest lactose that results in intestinal discomfort such as, cramps, flatulence, colic pains, abnormal intestinal flow, nausea and watery diarrhoea. These symptoms appear within 30-90 minutes after the ingestion of milk. It is important to remind that lactose intolerance is not a disease but a condition. To avoid this, fermented milk products such as yogurt and cheese should be used.

3. Glucose

Glucose is a simple carbohydrate. It is the most common and popular monosaccharide that can be found in sweet fruits such as grapes, which contains 20 – 30 % glucose. The carbohydrates you eat are converted to glucose in the body. The concentration of glucose in the blood, referred to as the blood glucose level, is vital to the proper functioning of the human body.

Some of the benefits and uses of glucose are,

It is mainly used by the living bodies for the production of instant energy.

It is an important constituent of human blood, human blood contains normally about 70 – 110mg of glucose per 100cm³.

It also regulates the temperature of the body.

The surplus glucose is converted to a polymer called glycogen in human beings. Glycogen is then stored in the liver and muscles. When the body is deficient in glucose, this liver and muscle glycogen is hydrolysed to glucose according to the body requirement.

The disadvantages related to the extra intake of glucose is,

Human pancreas secretes a hormone known as insulin. Insulin helps in the metabolism of glucose to produce energy. In some cases, defects in the metabolism of glucose occurs due to which blood glucose level rise from the normal level. This condition results in a disease known as diabetes mellitus. The consequences of unchecked diabetes include hardening of blood vessels, dysfunction of kidney, diabetic coma that causes premature death.

21.2 Proteins

The term protein is derived from the Greek word proteios, which means “first, prime or chief”. Proteins are naturally occurring polymers composed of amino acid units joined to one another by amide (or peptide) bonds. Spider webs, animal hair and muscle, egg whites and haemoglobin (the molecule that transports oxygen in the body to where it is needed) are all proteins. They are present in all animals, plants, bacteria and viruses.

Chemically, proteins are complex nitrogenous organic compounds, which are associated with the concept of life itself.

By chemical composition, proteins are composed of carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen. Percentage of nitrogen is fairly constant and is about 16% of the molecular weight of protein.
